props.title:
Inside Mem0:
Memory for AI Agents
props.subtitle: architecture · algorithms · benchmarks · the 2026 redesign

props.sub: every call starts from an empty context window

items.d: context windows, cost, kinds of memory

captions: Every conversation with an AI agent starts from
zero. It forgets your name, your plans, the
bug you fixed yesterday.
Mem0 is one of the most widely used
answers to that problem: a long-term memory layer
for agents.
In the next thirty minutes, we'll take it
apart, down to the formulas in the code.
Here's the core problem.
A language model is stateless. Each call sees
only what you put into its context window,
and nothing else.
So memory is not something the model has.
It's a system you build around the model.
That system must decide what to remember, how
to store it, how to find it again,
and what to do when facts change.
Those four decisions are exactly what this video
is about.
Here's the plan.
First, why agents need memory at all.
Then the architecture: the APIs, the stores, and
how data flows.
Then extract and update, the two-phase pipeline from
the twenty twenty five paper.
Then vectors and HNSW, the algorithm that finds
memories fast.
Then graph memory.
Then the benchmarks.
And finally, the twenty twenty six redesign, which
changed almost everything.
